name: fig-06
title: fig-06: The molecular interface
confidence_basis: Calibrated off Provisional (workbench 0.4.1): the four-channel coupling is robustly demonstrated on a deterministic 20-tick run -- the matter=>charge=>energy identities hold to 1e-30, the ATP:H+ stoichiometry and rotary torque are exact pins, and a zero-drive negative control plus the bare-draft contrast confirm the ramp is the driver -- but the BASELINE (fig06-runnable) is held at Medium, not High, because its constants are literature-plausible order-of-magnitude values and its transduction law is algebraic (no saturation/back-pressure), not a calibrated biophysical model. The MECHANISTIC VARIANT (fig06-mechanistic, scientific-review revision) materially raises the mechanistic support: torque and efficiency are now DERIVED rather than imposed (the derived τ_drive = n_c·e·Δp/2π = 38 pN·nm independently reproduces the measured ~40 pN·nm), stall and reversal are emergent outcomes of the torque balance with the full power budget closing to 1e-33 W, and a first-principles stall-gradient prediction (Δp* = 125 mV) is stated before the run and verified by a Δp sweep. The study is still held at Provisional overall because the mechanistic model is a reduced one-degree-of-freedom overdamped rotor (no explicit c-ring half-channels or elastic power-stroke) and is not yet fitted to a single enzyme's measured speed-vs-load curve.
question: Does the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) hold as a runnable process -- a molecular mechanism (F₁Fₒ ATP synthase) that exchanges matter and energy through a small set of TYPED physical channels (chemical mol·s⁻¹, electrical C·s⁻¹, mechanical torque N·m, thermal J·s⁻¹) with NO cell-level boundary, all four channels driven from ONE coupled proton flux so matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy are conserved across the interface?
biological_summary:
This is the executable realization of the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface). The paper's point is that at the molecular level interactions are governed directly by molecular processes rather than by a maintained cell-level boundary: molecules exchange matter, energy, and momentum through a small set of physical channels -- chemical exchange, electrostatics, mechanical forces, and thermal fluctuations (Fig molecular_interface a) -- and a molecular interface must expose exactly these as typed ports over molecular structure (Fig molecular_interface b), with no cell boundary.
The runnable composite (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.fig06-runnable`) names the mechanism: the F₁Fₒ ATP synthase as a four-channel transducer (`MolecularMechanismHandler`). A `ProtonMotiveRamp` charges the substrate/proton drive (`chemical_in`) linearly over the run -- the fig06 analogue of fig04's diffusing gradient -- so the driving proton flux sweeps upward. From that ONE coupled quantity the mechanism produces four TYPED physical outputs: an ATP synthesis flux (chemical, `J_ATP = k_cat·activity`), the proton current carried across the proton-motive force (electrical, `I = J_ATP·n·e`), a near-constant rotary torque on the Fₒ rotor (mechanical, `τ ≈ 40 pN·nm = 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m`), and the non-conserved remainder dissipated as heat (thermal, `Q = (1−η)·PMF power`, η = 0.75). Because all four derive from the single proton flux, the interface is physically consistent: matter⇒charge coupling (`I = J_ATP·n·e`) and charge⇒energy coupling (`Q = (1−η)·I·pmf`) hold exactly on every step, and the PMF input power splits into a conserved useful fraction and the dissipated remainder (`w_pmf = η·w_pmf + Q`).
The literature constants (k_cat ≈ 100 ATP·s⁻¹, H⁺/ATP ≈ 3.3, |Δp| ≈ 150 mV, Fₒ torque ≈ 40 pN·nm, η ≈ 75 %) live in `config`, and the mechanical channel deliberately carries TORQUE (N·m), not force or power -- the drive sets the rotor's speed, not its torque, so torque holds near-constant while the chemical/electrical/thermal channels scale with the drive. The composite runs 20 ticks through the process-bigraph engine and every output channel is a deterministic function of the ramped drive, so the whole trajectory reproduces exactly run to run. There is no cell-level boundary anywhere in the state -- only the molecular mechanism, its ramp driver, and the typed ports over molecular structure.
claim: The F₁Fₒ ATP synthase modeled as a single molecular process with four TYPED physical ports (chemical `chemical_flux`, electrical `current`, mechanical `torque`, thermal `heat_flux`) over a `structure` leaf -- and NO cell boundary -- reproduces the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) as a runnable transducer: driven by one ramped proton flux, the mechanism emits an ATP synthesis flux that scales linearly with the drive (`J_ATP = k_cat·activity`, exactly 4× flux for 4× activity), a proton current fixed to that flux at the ATP:H⁺ = 1/3.3 stoichiometry on every step, a near-constant rotary torque of 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m, and a dissipated heat exactly equal to (1−η)·PMF-power = 25 % of input power -- so matter (chemical), charge (electrical), angular momentum (mechanical), and energy (thermal) are conserved across one coupled interface, all four channels derived from the single proton flux, all deterministic and reproducible run to run.

variants.name: fig06-mechanistic
variants.rationale: Real-mechanism upgrade (scientific-review revision, Oct 2026). Where the fig06-runnable baseline *imposes* a 40 pN·nm torque and a 75 % efficiency as fixed constants, this variant builds a genuine reduced rotary-motor model (AtpSynthaseRotor, handlers_fig06_mech.py): a single overdamped rotational degree of freedom driven by the proton-motive force Δp against the ATP back-torque τ_chem = n_ATP·ΔG_ATP/2π and an external load τ_ext. Torque, speed, proton/ATP flux, the power split, efficiency, stall and reversal are all DERIVED outcomes, not settings. Notably the derived drive torque τ_drive = n_c·e·Δp/2π = 38 pN·nm at Δp = 150 mV REPRODUCES the ~40 pN·nm the baseline merely imposed, and the power budget P_in = P_ATP + P_ext + P_heat closes to 1e-33 W on every step. The baseline fig06-runnable is kept intact as the algebraic didactic smoke test (software baseline), per the review's additive-variant mandate.

key_assumptions: This `fig06-runnable` composite is a **didactic / toy-real** transducer, not a calibrated biophysical model of ATP synthase. Its constants (k_cat ≈ 100 ATP·s⁻¹, H⁺/ATP ≈ 3.3, |Δp| ≈ 150 mV, Fₒ torque ≈ 40 pN·nm, η ≈ 75 %) are literature-plausible order-of-magnitude values placed in `config`, chosen to make the four-channel coupling legible over a 20-tick run -- NOT fitted to a specific enzyme, membrane potential, or measured turnover curve.

The four output channels are computed by an algebraic transduction law, not a mechanistic rotary kinetics model: `J_ATP = k_cat·activity` is strictly linear (no saturation / Michaelis–Menten rollover, no back-pressure from a proton-motive force that depletes), the ATP:H⁺ ratio is a fixed constant, and the torque is a fixed leaf value. This is the paper's point (a molecular interface exposes typed coupled channels) rendered minimally, not a claim about the enzyme's true rate law.

The mechanical channel deliberately carries TORQUE (N·m), not force (N) or power (W) -- the drive sets the Fₒ rotor's rotational speed (ω = 2π·J_H/c-ring), not its torque, so torque holds near-constant with load while the other three channels scale with the drive. This was a deliberate modeling choice matching the draft's declared `mechanical_out: torque` port; the caption's "mechanical forces" is realized here specifically as rotary torque.

There is NO cell-level boundary, membrane compartment, or spatial lattice in the composite state -- only the molecular mechanism, its `ProtonMotiveRamp` driver, and the typed ports over a `structure` leaf. That absence is deliberate: it is exactly the paper's Fig molecular_interface b point (typed ports over molecular structure, with no cell-level boundary).

The `ProtonMotiveRamp` charges the drive by a fixed positive increment each tick (drive_rate = 0.06), a scripted monotonic driver standing in for a real, self-consistently maintained proton-motive force. The environment→transducer coupling it makes legible is real; the ramp shape itself is scripted, not emergent.

The `structure` port is a read-only string leaf (a PDB/SMILES-style identifier) and does not enter the dynamics -- it stands for the molecular structure the interface is defined over, not a simulated conformation.
acceptance_criteria: The ATP synthesis flux (chemical channel) is strictly positive under drive and scales linearly with the proton drive -- 4× the activity gives exactly 4× the ATP flux, and rises monotonically as the ramp charges the drive over the run.

The four typed channels are ONE coupled quantity, not four free knobs -- the electrical channel is the chemical channel carried as charge (`I = J_ATP·n·e`, matter⇒charge) and the thermal channel is the fixed remainder of the electrical channel's PMF power (`Q = (1−η)·I·pmf`, charge⇒energy), exactly on every step.
The ATP:H⁺ stoichiometry holds at 1/n_protons_per_atp (1/3.3) on every active step -- matter and charge are conserved together across the chemical and electrical ports.
The rotary torque (mechanical channel) is strictly positive and holds near-constant at the configured 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m (40 pN·nm) -- torque, not force or power, and independent of the drive level.

The electrical energy balance closes -- dissipated heat equals (1−η)·input PMF power (= 25 % of input), useful work is the conserved η-fraction, and both are non-negative -- energy conserved across the interface.

units_and_time.time: 1 tick = 1 unit interval of dimensionless model time; the run is 20 ticks (21 emitted rows, t=0..20).
units_and_time.quantities: chemical channel J_ATP in ATP·s⁻¹ (mol·s⁻¹ analogue); electrical channel I in amperes (C·s⁻¹) via proton_charge e = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C; mechanical channel torque in N·m (40 pN·nm = 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m); thermal channel heat in watts (J·s⁻¹); proton-motive force pmf = 0.15 V. The substrate/proton drive `chemical_in` is a dimensionless activity that ramps 0.2 → 1.34 over the run at drive_rate 0.06/tick.
units_and_time.note: Constants are literature-plausible order-of-magnitude values in `config`, not calibrated to a specific enzyme or membrane -- the units are physically typed and internally consistent, the magnitudes are toy-real.

measure.expr: J_ATP driven directly at activity 0.3 vs 1.2, and over the ramped run

behavior_tests.description: Negative control (not the figure's scientific claim, a soundness check): with zero substrate/proton drive the mechanism transduces nothing -- the chemical, electrical, and thermal outputs are exactly zero (the mechanism does not manufacture flux without a proton-motive force). The mechanical torque leaf is a fixed motor property and is excluded.

pass_if.provenance: driving the handler at zero activity yields chemical_out == electrical_out == thermal_out == 0.0 exactly -- a driven transducer, not a spontaneous source; the constant mechanical torque leaf is a fixed port property and is deliberately excluded (tests/test_fig06_atp_synthase.py::test_zero_drive_yields_zero_flux_on_every_channel)

behavior_tests.name: mech-power-budget-closes
behavior_tests.description: The full power budget closes exactly on every step: the proton-motive input power equals the chemical power stored in ATP plus the mechanical work done against the load plus the viscous heat, P_in = P_ATP + P_ext + P_heat. Energy is conserved across the rotary interface by construction (multiply the torque balance by ω), not asserted by an imposed efficiency.

measure.expr: max |P_in − (P_ATP + P_ext + P_heat)| over the 20-tick run

pass_if.provenance: INVARIANT. Observed max residual 3.1e-33 W over the live 20-tick fig06-mechanistic run — machine precision. Unlike the baseline's imposed 75/25 split, here the useful fraction is an outcome of the operating point (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_power_budget_closes_every_step, ::test_dissipated_heat_is_nonnegative, ::test_charge_current_identity_holds_every_step)

behavior_tests.name: mech-torque-derived-matches-literature
behavior_tests.description: The rotary drive torque is DERIVED from the proton-motive force, τ_drive = n_c·e·Δp/2π, and at Δp = 150 mV lands at ≈ 38 pN·nm — reproducing the ~40 pN·nm the baseline merely imposed as a fixed leaf. It scales linearly with Δp (doubling the pmf doubles the torque), proving it is a derived quantity, not a constant.

measure.expr: τ_drive at Δp = 150 mV vs the n_c·e·Δp/2π prediction, and the τ(2Δp)/τ(Δp) ratio

pass_if.value: 38.2e-21 N·m (35–42 pN·nm literature band); linear-in-Δp ratio = 2.0
pass_if.provenance: EMPIRICAL_COMPARISON against the measured Fₒ stall torque of the bacterial/chloroplast synthase (~40 pN·nm; Junge & Nelson 2015). Observed 38.2 pN·nm exactly equal to n_c·e·Δp/2π, and τ(0.2V)/τ(0.1V) = 2.000 (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_drive_torque_derived_matches_literature, ::test_drive_torque_scales_with_pmf_not_fixed)

behavior_tests.name: mech-load-induces-stall-and-reversal
behavior_tests.description: As the external load ramps, the rotor turns forward (synthesising ATP), slows, STALLS when τ_ext = τ_drive − τ_chem (≈ tick 11), then REVERSES (ω < 0) — running as an ATP-driven proton pump. ω and J_ATP flip sign together; past stall the proton current also reverses (protons pumped against the gradient). Direction is an outcome of the load, not a scripted schedule.

measure.expr: sign(ω) over the load ramp; co-sign of ω and J_ATP; reversal pumps J_H < 0

pass_if.value: ω crosses 0 at ~tick 11 and goes < −100; in reversal J_ATP < 0 and J_H < 0
pass_if.provenance: MECHANISTIC_ABLATION (counterfactual on the shaft load). Observed forward ω peak +654, stall at tick 11, reversal to ω −597 by tick 20; at τ_ext = 1.2e-20 N·m the rotor runs backward with J_ATP < 0 (hydrolysis) and proton current < 0 (pumping) together (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_load_ramp_drives_forward_stall_reversal, ::test_reversal_pumps_protons_and_hydrolyses_atp)

behavior_tests.name: mech-proton-gradient-sets-direction
behavior_tests.description: A first-principles prediction: synthesis proceeds iff n_c·e·Δp > n_ATP·ΔG_ATP, so the stall gradient Δp* = n_ATP·ΔG_ATP/(n_c·e) can be computed BEFORE running. Verified by sweeping Δp: below Δp* the motor reverses (hydrolysis), at Δp* it stalls, above it synthesises. The sensitivity is to the proton gradient itself, not merely to a driver ramp.

measure.path: obs.omega over a Δp sweep (20–300 mV)
measure.expr: sign(ω) vs the predicted threshold Δp* = n_ATP·ΔG_ATP/(n_c·e)

pass_if.value: Δp* ≈ 125 mV; ω<0 below, ω≈0 at, ω>0 above
pass_if.provenance: PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION. Δp* = 125 mV computed from the pool thermodynamics before the run; the Δp sweep then shows ω < 0 at 95 mV, |ω| < 1 at 125 mV, ω > 0 at 155 mV — direction set by the gradient, as predicted (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_pmf_threshold_sets_direction)

behavior_tests.name: mech-efficiency-is-derived-not-imposed
behavior_tests.description: The chemical efficiency η = P_ATP/P_in = τ_chem/τ_drive is a DERIVED outcome that varies with the operating point — a higher proton-motive force gives a lower chemical-storage fraction — and is not the baseline's imposed 0.75. This is the direct answer to the review's point that the baseline's 75 % efficiency is prescribed.

measure.expr: η(Δp=150mV) vs η(Δp=300mV); distance from the imposed 0.75

pass_if.provenance: MECHANISTIC_ABLATION. Observed η = 0.833 at 150 mV, falling at 300 mV (more of the proton power spent as kinetic/viscous rather than stored) — bounded, operating-point dependent, and distinct from the imposed 0.75 baseline constant (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_efficiency_is_derived_and_varies_with_pmf)

behavior_tests.name: mech-atp-backpressure-slows-rotor
behavior_tests.description: With the ADP/ATP/Pi pools unbuffered, synthesised ATP accumulates, the reaction quotient and ΔG_ATP climb, and the rotor slows monotonically under its own product back-pressure — no external load applied. Honest scope: it slows, it does not reach a full static head over the window (ΔG rises only logarithmically with [ATP]); the baseline's strictly-linear J_ATP has no such feedback at all.

measure.path: obs.omega, obs.dg_atp over an 80-tick unbuffered run
measure.expr: ω monotone non-increasing while ΔG_ATP and [ATP] rise

pass_if.value: ω[-1] < ω[0], ΔG_ATP rises, [ATP] accumulates, ω non-increasing
pass_if.provenance: MECHANISTIC_ABLATION (product inhibition). Observed ω falling monotonically as ATP accumulates and ΔG_ATP rises across an 80-tick unbuffered run — real thermodynamic back-pressure, absent from the algebraic baseline (tests/test_fig06_mechanistic.py::test_atp_backpressure_slows_rotor)

findings.statement: A molecular mechanism (F₁Fₒ ATP synthase) modeled as a single process with four typed physical ports over a `structure` leaf -- and no cell boundary -- reproduces the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) as a runnable transducer. Driven by one ramped proton flux, it emits an ATP synthesis flux that scales linearly with the drive (4× activity ⇒ exactly 4× flux; monotone rise 20.0 → 128.0 over the run), a proton current fixed to that flux at ATP:H⁺ = 1/3.3 on every step, a near-constant 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m rotary torque, and a dissipated heat equal to (1−η)·PMF power. Confirmed deterministically across the 20-tick run.

evidence.observed: I == J_ATP·3.3·e and heat == 0.25·(I·pmf) exactly every step; ATP flux 20.0 → 128.0; torque 4.0×10⁻²⁰ N·m constant

findings.statement: The four typed channels are ONE coupled quantity, not four independent knobs: matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy are conserved together across the interface. The electrical channel is the chemical channel carried as charge (I = J_ATP·n·e), the thermal channel is the fixed (1−η) remainder of the electrical PMF power (energy balance: input power = useful + heat, 75 % / 25 % split), and the ATP:H⁺ stoichiometry holds at 1/3.3 exactly on every step. All coupling identities hold to 1e-30 on the live run -- the interface is physically consistent, not four separately scripted traces.

evidence.observed: J_ATP/J_H == 1/3.3 == 0.30303 every step; heat == 25 % of input power, useful == 75 %, both ≥ 0

findings.statement: The ATP-flux sweep is produced by the proton-drive ramp, not by the rate law itself -- shown by contrasting the bare figure draft against the driven transducer. The bare draft `fig06-executable` pins the substrate/proton activity at chemical_in = 1.0 and so reports a FLAT ATP turnover of chemical_out = 100.0 = k_cat (no ProtonMotiveRamp wired; its electrical, mechanical, and thermal output channels read 0.0 in the bare draft). Adding the ramp in `fig06-runnable` charges chemical_in from 0.2 to ~1.34, and because J_ATP = k_cat * activity the ATP flux then sweeps 20.0 -> 128.0 over the run while all four channels co-fire. The sweep is therefore the environment->transducer coupling (the ramp driving the proton flux), not an intrinsic nonlinearity of the mechanism -- the paper's point that at the molecular level interactions are governed by the driving flux, made measurable. Verified in-memory (workbench 0.4.1): fig06-executable chemical_out flat 100.0; fig06-runnable chemical_out 20.0 at first drive, rising linearly with activity.

evidence.observed: fig06-executable chemical_out flat 100.0 (= k_cat, activity pinned 1.0), other out channels 0.0; fig06-runnable chemical_out 20.0 -> 128.0 as the ramp charges activity 0.2 -> ~1.34

findings.statement: The baseline's TWO imposed constants become DERIVED, validated outcomes in the mechanistic variant. The rotary drive torque is τ_drive = n_c·e·Δp/2π — a consequence of n_c protons each delivering e·Δp of work per revolution — and at Δp = 150 mV it equals 38.2 pN·nm, reproducing the measured ~40 pN·nm Fₒ stall torque (Junge & Nelson 2015) that fig06-runnable merely set by hand. It scales linearly with the proton-motive force (τ(2Δp)/τ(Δp) = 2.000), so it is a derived function of Δp, not a leaf value. This directly answers the review's "fixed torque is imposed" objection: the number is now predicted from the gradient and matches experiment.

evidence.observed: τ_drive = 38.2 pN·nm at 150 mV = n_c·e·Δp/2π exactly; linear-in-Δp ratio 2.000

findings.statement: Stall and reversal are EMERGENT outcomes of the torque balance, not scripted events. Ramping the external shaft load drives the rotor forward (synthesis), through a stall where τ_ext = τ_drive − τ_chem (≈ tick 11), and into reversal (ω < 0) where it runs backward as an ATP-driven proton pump — J_ATP and the proton current both flip sign with ω. Throughout, the full power budget P_in = P_ATP + P_ext + P_heat closes to 3.1e-33 W (machine precision), with viscous dissipation P_heat = ζω² ≥ 0 — so the machine is thermodynamically reversible and energy-conserving by construction, not by an imposed efficiency. The baseline could not represent stall, reversal, or load at all.

evidence.observed: forward ω +654 → stall tick 11 → reversal ω −597; J_ATP<0 & J_H<0 in reversal; power residual ≤ 3.1e-33 W

findings.statement: The model makes a genuine prospective prediction and passes it. Synthesis proceeds iff n_c·e·Δp > n_ATP·ΔG_ATP, so the stall gradient Δp* = n_ATP·ΔG_ATP/(n_c·e) = 125 mV can be computed BEFORE any run. Sweeping the proton-motive force then confirms it: ω < 0 (hydrolysis) below Δp*, ω ≈ 0 at Δp*, ω > 0 (synthesis) above. Direction is set by the proton gradient relative to the ATP free energy — the thermodynamic directionality the review asked for — demonstrated as a predicted threshold, not a fitted curve.

evidence.observed: Δp* = 125 mV predicted from pool thermodynamics; sweep ω<0 at 95 mV, ≈0 at 125 mV, >0 at 155 mV

findings.statement: The efficiency is a derived, operating-point-dependent outcome, and the pools provide real back-pressure — with the limits stated honestly. η = P_ATP/P_in = τ_chem/τ_drive = 0.833 at 150 mV and falls as Δp rises (more proton power spent as rotation/viscous loss), so it is not the baseline's imposed 0.75. With the ADP/ATP/Pi pools unbuffered, accumulating ATP raises ΔG_ATP and slows the rotor monotonically (product inhibition) — a feedback the strictly-linear baseline lacks entirely. Honest scope: this is still a reduced one-degree-of-freedom model (no explicit c-ring half-channels, no elastic power-stroke, overdamped, pool_coupling is a convenience scale), and the back-pressure slows but does not fully stall the rotor over the tested window.

evidence.observed: η 0.833 at 150 mV, lower at 300 mV, ≠ 0.75; ω monotone-decreasing as [ATP]/ΔG_ATP rise (unbuffered)

explanatory_gain.basis: Rendering the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure as a runnable transducer makes its central claim concrete and checkable: a molecular mechanism exposes a small set of TYPED physical channels (chemical, electrical, mechanical torque, thermal) over molecular structure with no cell-level boundary, and those channels are coupled -- one proton flux drives all four with matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy conserved. The figure is executable, not merely drawn.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The F₁Fₒ ATP synthase modeled as a single molecular process with four TYPED physical ports (chemical, electrical, mechanical torque, thermal) over a `structure` leaf -- and NO cell boundary -- reproduces the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) as a runnable transducer. Driven by one ramped proton flux over a 20-tick run: the ATP synthesis flux scales linearly with the drive (4× activity ⇒ exactly 4× flux; monotone 20.0 → 128.0), the proton current is fixed to that flux at ATP:H⁺ = 1/3.3 on every step, the rotary torque holds constant at 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m, and the dissipated heat equals (1−η)·PMF power (25 % of input). All readouts are deterministic and reproduce exactly.
- The four channels are ONE coupled quantity, not four free knobs -- the coupling identities (I = J_ATP·n·e for matter⇒charge, Q = (1−η)·I·pmf for charge⇒energy) hold exactly to 1e-30 on the live run, so matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy are conserved across the interface. The energy balance closes at a 75 %/25 % useful/dissipated split.
- There is no cell-level boundary anywhere in the state -- only the mechanism, its ramp driver, and the typed ports over molecular structure -- which is exactly the Fig molecular_interface b point.

## Evidence
- **ATP-FLUX-SCALES-WITH-THE-PROTON-DRIVE** -- J_ATP = k_cat·activity exactly (ratio 4.0 for 4× drive); monotone rise 20.0 → 128.0
- **FOUR-CHANNELS-DERIVE-FROM-ONE-PROTON-FLUX** -- I == J_ATP·3.3·e and heat == 0.25·(I·pmf) exactly (1e-30) every step; all four co-fire under drive
- **ATP-PROTON-STOICHIOMETRY-CONSERVED** -- J_ATP/J_H == 1/3.3 == 0.30303 on every active step
- **ROTARY-TORQUE-HOLDS-NEAR-CONSTANT** -- mechanical_out == 4.0×10⁻²⁰ N·m exactly, constant while the other channels scale
- **ELECTRICAL-ENERGY-BALANCE-CLOSES** -- heat == 25 % of input PMF power, useful == 75 %, both ≥ 0
- **NO-DRIVE-NO-SPONTANEOUS-FLUX** -- all three flux channels == 0.0 at zero drive (negative control)
- **BARE-DRAFT-IS-FLAT-VS-DRIVEN-SWEEP** (companion executable, workbench 0.4.1) -- the un-driven draft fig06-executable reports a flat chemical_out == 100.0 (= k_cat, activity pinned 1.0), while the ramp-driven fig06-runnable sweeps chemical_out 20.0 -> 128.0; the sweep is the drive coupling, not the rate law

## Limitations
- This is a didactic / toy-real transducer, not a calibrated biophysical model: the constants are literature-plausible order-of-magnitude values, and the transduction law is algebraic (strictly linear J_ATP, fixed stoichiometry, fixed torque leaf), with no saturation or PMF back-pressure.
- The mechanical channel is realized specifically as rotary torque (N·m), a deliberate choice matching the draft's `mechanical_out: torque` port; the caption's "mechanical forces" appears here as torque, not force or power.
- The rigorous molecular-scale cousin is `molecular-interfaces` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation -- see limitations; this study does not restate its numbers as its own.

## Next steps
- Add saturation / Michaelis–Menten kinetics and a self-consistent proton-motive force with back-pressure, so the ATP flux rolls over rather than rising linearly without bound.
- Couple this molecular interface into a cell-level composite to show the same typed ports composing across scales (the QM/MM and integrative-structural-modeling composition the paper cites).

limitations: This `fig06-runnable` composite is a didactic / toy-real transducer, not a calibrated biophysical model of ATP synthase. Its constants (k_cat ≈ 100 ATP·s⁻¹, H⁺/ATP ≈ 3.3, |Δp| ≈ 150 mV, Fₒ torque ≈ 40 pN·nm, η ≈ 75 %) are literature-plausible order-of-magnitude values in `config`, chosen to make the four-channel coupling legible over a 20-tick run -- not fitted to a specific enzyme, membrane potential, or measured turnover curve.

The transduction law is algebraic, not a mechanistic rotary-kinetics model -- J_ATP = k_cat·activity is strictly linear (no Michaelis–Menten saturation, no proton-motive-force back-pressure), the ATP:H⁺ ratio is a fixed constant, and the torque is a fixed leaf value. This renders the paper''s typed-coupled-channels point minimally, not the enzyme''s true rate law.

The mechanical channel deliberately carries torque (N·m), not force (N) or power (W) -- the drive sets the rotor's speed, not its torque. The caption's "mechanical forces" is realized here specifically as rotary torque, matching the draft's declared `mechanical_out` torque port (N·m).

The `ProtonMotiveRamp` is a scripted monotonic driver (drive_rate 0.06/tick), standing in for a real, self-consistently maintained proton-motive force. The environment→transducer coupling it makes legible is real; the ramp shape itself is scripted, not emergent.
The `structure` port is a read-only string identifier and does not enter the dynamics -- it stands for the molecular structure the interface is defined over, not a simulated conformation.

The rigorous molecular-scale cousin is `molecular-interfaces` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation, which treats the molecular interface at higher fidelity; this study is the deliberately minimal, runnable figure-carrier and does not restate that study's numbers as its own.

Mechanistic variant (fig06-mechanistic) — scope and honest limits: it is a REDUCED one-rotational-degree-of-freedom overdamped model (ω = net_torque/ζ), not a full rotary-kinetics simulation. It does not resolve the c-ring half-channel proton-binding steps, the elastic power-stroke, rotational substeps, or thermal/Brownian ratcheting; the rotational drag ζ and the pool_coupling scale are chosen for legibility, not fitted. The derived torque matches the literature stall torque, but the model is NOT yet calibrated to a specific enzyme's measured speed-vs-load (torque-velocity) curve — that empirical_comparison is the next step. The ATP back-pressure slows the rotor but does not reach a full static head over the tested window.
falsifiability: Overturned if the ATP flux fails to scale linearly with the proton drive, if any of the coupling identities (I = J_ATP·n·e, Q = (1−η)·I·pmf) fails on the live run, if the ATP:H⁺ stoichiometry drifts off 1/3.3, if the rotary torque is not constant or begins scaling with the drive (implying a force/power channel rather than torque), if the energy balance fails to close at the (η, 1−η) split, or if a zero drive produces a non-zero flux on any of the three driven channels.

config.caption: The paper's panel-b diagram — a molecular mechanism exposing physical ports (chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal, structural) with molecular subports.

Baseline (didactic smoke test): the simpler pre-revision transducer (fig06-runnable), kept as the executable baseline. The F₁Fₒ ATP synthase driven by a proton-motive-force ramp — from the ONE coupled proton flux (drive, dashed) it produces four TYPED physical channels: ATP synthesis flux (chemical), proton current (electrical), a near-constant rotary torque on the Fₒ rotor (mechanical), and dissipated heat (thermal). What to look for: ATP flux scaling with the drive at the fixed ATP:H⁺ = 1/3.3 stoichiometry, and the energy balance holding (heat = (1−η)·input power). NOTE — here torque (≈40 pN·nm) and efficiency (η = 0.75) are IMPOSED constants; the mechanistic figure below derives them from the physics.

Mechanistic (the decisive figure): a real reduced rotary F₁Fₒ motor in which every physical quantity is DERIVED from the proton-motive force Δp, the ATP free energy ΔG_ATP, and the shaft load. (A) the rotor shaft turns — cumulative revolutions rise under synthesis, peak at stall, then fall as it reverses. (B) angular velocity ω and ATP flux J_ATP cross zero together at the stall (tick 11) and go negative (reversal/hydrolysis). (C) torque balance: the derived drive torque τ_drive = n_c·e·Δp/2π ≈ 38 pN·nm (matching the measured ~40) against the ATP back-torque and the ramped external load; τ_net crosses zero at stall. (D) the power budget closes exactly, P_in = P_ATP + P_ext + P_heat (the dotted sum overlies P_in). (E) sweeping the proton-motive force sets direction about the first-principles stall gradient Δp* = n_ATP·ΔG_ATP/(n_c·e) = 125 mV — synthesis above, hydrolysis below. (F) the external load throttles the ATP flux relative to the unloaded motor. From scripts/build_fig06_mechanistic.py.

experiment: Run the `fig06-runnable` composite (MolecularMechanismHandler -- the F₁Fₒ ATP synthase as a four-channel transducer -- driven by a ProtonMotiveRamp charging the substrate/proton drive linearly) to completion over 20 ticks through the process-bigraph engine, and measure whether one coupled proton flux drives four TYPED physical channels (chemical ATP flux, electrical proton current, mechanical rotary torque, thermal heat) with matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy conserved across a molecular interface that has no cell-level boundary.
result: Over a deterministic 20-tick run, the F₁Fₒ ATP synthase transducer drives four TYPED physical channels from ONE ramped proton flux, with no cell-level boundary in the state. The chemical channel (ATP synthesis flux) scales linearly with the drive -- 4× activity gives exactly 4× flux (30.0 at activity 0.3, 120.0 at 1.2), rising monotonically 20.0 → 128.0 over the run. The four channels are one coupled quantity: the proton current is the ATP flux carried as charge (I = J_ATP·n·e), the ATP:H⁺ stoichiometry holds at 1/3.3 exactly on every step, the rotary torque holds constant at 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m (torque, not force/power -- the drive sets speed, not torque), and the dissipated heat equals (1−η)·PMF power = 25 % of input, useful work 75 %, both non-negative. All coupling identities hold to 1e-30 on the live run and every readout reproduces exactly. A zero drive produces zero flux on all three driven channels (negative control), and the un-driven bare draft fig06-executable reports a flat chemical_out of 100.0 (= k_cat) whereas the ramp-driven fig06-runnable sweeps 20.0 -> 128.0 -- confirming the sweep is the drive coupling, not the rate law (workbench 0.4.1). The paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) holds as a runnable process: a molecular mechanism exposing typed, coupled chemical/electrical/mechanical/thermal channels over molecular structure, matter/charge/ angular-momentum/energy conserved across the interface, with no cell boundary -- executable, not merely drawn. The rigorous molecular-scale cousin is `molecular-interfaces` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.
